purpose: The templates band of a solution page: a framed media split whose copy side invites the reader to start from a template and whose media side is a scrolling two-column wall of deployable template cards, closed by a marquee of the frameworks and clouds it works with. Each card is a mark, a title, one line and a deploy action. It is a page section — the site places it from a `{ _id: 'template-gallery', props }` entry and binds `props` straight onto it — so its whole API is the props below, and it composes `section-module`, `media-split`, `scroll-area`, `card-grid`, `button`, `registration-frame` and `marquee` rather than owning any anatomy of its own. With `closing` set it is the page's closing band: the hatched closing frame follows it, with no rules of its own, because the site footer under it opens with one (`hatch` turns that frame off when another closing band stacks directly below and draws the shared one).
useWhen: Use TemplateGallery on marketing pages to show deployable templates; set `closing` when it is the last band.
On a solution page (Retail, Web Apps, AI Workloads, Security, Performance, Streaming) to show the templates a reader can deploy right away.
Whenever a band pairs one pitch with a long, browsable list of deployable starters.
avoidWhen: For a grid of features with artwork → use `feature-tiles`.
For a marquee of marks alone → compose `marquee` directly.
For a handful of icon-led use cases → use `customer-use-cases`.
For a closing ask with links or a command and no templates → use `closing-call-to-action`; for an email sign-up close → use `newsletter-section`.
related: `media-split` — the framed copy-and-media split the band is built on; it owns the band's named region.
`marquee` — the row of framework and cloud marks that closes the band.
bestPractices: Keep the wall to an even number of templates so the two columns end level.
Turn on `invertInDark` only for a mark whose artwork ships in dark ink, so it stays legible on the dark theme.
Set `templatesAriaLabel` so the scrolling wall is announced by name.

Set `closing` only on the last band of the page, right above `site-footer`: it draws the hatched closing frame itself, so nothing follows it inside the page column (no trailing `SectionGap`, no closing `RegistrationFrame`).
Turn `hatch` off only on a closing band that another closing band follows directly; the last one keeps the frame.
